Telegraph and telephone service-
488.	Administration, operation and maintenance, $1,566,380.

maintopic: ANNOUNCEMENT OF APPOINTMENT OF THE CHIEF JUSTICE OF CANADA, THE SPEAKER OF THE SENATE, THE SPEAKER OF THE HOUSE OF COMMONS AND THE LEADER OF THE OPPOSITION
speechtext:
I should like to ask the Minister of Transport whether he can give us any information as to the progress of the negotiations which we all know have been going on between the dominion government telegraph and telephones on the one hand and the Canadian National Railways-that is, Canadian National Telegraphs-and the British Columbia Telephone Company on the other hand, with a view to the dominion selling the telephone and telegraph services in northern British Columbia, thereby integrating that part of the province with the commercial services of the rest of Canada and, I think it may safely be said, at the same time bringing up to modern commercial standards the services to the communities of that area?

Supply-Transport

maintopic: ANNOUNCEMENT OF APPOINTMENT OF THE CHIEF JUSTICE OF CANADA, THE SPEAKER OF THE SENATE, THE SPEAKER OF THE HOUSE OF COMMONS AND THE LEADER OF THE OPPOSITION
speechtext: Yes. Negotiations have been carried on between the Department of Transport and the British Columbia Telephone Company and the Canadian National Telegraphs. The latter company made a substantial offer -which I should not like to mention at this time, if that is agreeable, and which I think we would be disposed to accept-for all the facilities having to do with telegraph operations in the province of British Columbia. On the other hand, so far as telephone facilities are concerned, on several occasions I have seen officers of the British Columbia Telephone Company or their representatives, but I am not in a position to make any announcement as to an agreed purchase price. There have been several discussions as to amounts, but none upon which we could agree. Rather than affect the discussions in any way I would prefer, if my hon. friend would allow it, not to say any more about the matter.

maintopic: ANNOUNCEMENT OF APPOINTMENT OF THE CHIEF JUSTICE OF CANADA, THE SPEAKER OF THE SENATE, THE SPEAKER OF THE HOUSE OF COMMONS AND THE LEADER OF THE OPPOSITION
speechtext: Negotiations are going on?

maintopic: ANNOUNCEMENT OF APPOINTMENT OF THE CHIEF JUSTICE OF CANADA, THE SPEAKER OF THE SENATE, THE SPEAKER OF THE HOUSE OF COMMONS AND THE LEADER OF THE OPPOSITION
speechtext:
Yes. Negotiations are
going on.

maintopic: ANNOUNCEMENT OF APPOINTMENT OF THE CHIEF JUSTICE OF CANADA, THE SPEAKER OF THE SENATE, THE SPEAKER OF THE HOUSE OF COMMONS AND THE LEADER OF THE OPPOSITION
speechtext:
In that connection may I say that it is good to learn that the intention is to bring the telephone and telegraphic services in the interior of British Columbia up to a high degree of efficiency. I should like to say to the minister that, regardless of any agreement which is made with any of these companies, there will remain the claim of ranchers 80 miles or 100 miles out, miners, settlers and so on, who depend upon this communication system for their very existence.
When British Columbia entered confederation in 1871 that was one of the main points taken into consideration in the agreement with Canada. Commitments made at that time, regardless of any decisions made now, must be carried out. Let us take the case of a rancher a hundred miles out from the rail, in a little community at the end of a trail. In times past the telegraph or telephone system of this government has serviced that little community, and it was available to save life or limb, or to bring relief. It was not operated on a cash and carry basis. Today in the Cariboo country we have hundreds of miles of these telegraph and telephone lines leading out into the remote areas. Neither the British Columbia Telephone Company, the Bell Telephone Company nor anybody else would be able to make any revenue from that service. Nevertheless it is necessary and vital to the success of that country.
We are most fortunate in having a minister who realizes the humanitarian aspect of the matter as well as the cash and carry side of
[Mr. Applewhaite.l
the communications service in that great part of British Columbia which is progressing so rapidly and emerging from pioneer status to that of a commercial area in Canada. New towns in that area are growing up with 1,000 telephones, or 500 or 400 as the case may be. A decision has to be made as to whether this service will be carried on under the crown or whether we will sell it to a private industry.

maintopic: ANNOUNCEMENT OF APPOINTMENT OF THE CHIEF JUSTICE OF CANADA, THE SPEAKER OF THE SENATE, THE SPEAKER OF THE HOUSE OF COMMONS AND THE LEADER OF THE OPPOSITION
speechtext: I should like to endorse the remarks of the hon. member for Cariboo. It is vital that the service to the people living in the more remote parts of the interior of the province should not be discontinued. Perhaps the minister would tell us whether it is the intention of the government to have, as a term in any agreement made with the British Columbia Telephone Company, the provision that services of this type will be maintained.

maintopic: ANNOUNCEMENT OF APPOINTMENT OF THE CHIEF JUSTICE OF CANADA, THE SPEAKER OF THE SENATE, THE SPEAKER OF THE HOUSE OF COMMONS AND THE LEADER OF THE OPPOSITION
speechtext: There are two things that should be considered in these negotiations. The first is that these services are operated by the Department of Transport in isolated communities at a considerable loss. That has been the policy of the department not only in British Columbia but elsewhere in Canada, But when it becomes evident that these services can be made to pay, it is only natural that we should want to dispose of them, particularly when we can dispose of them at a profit. That is what we have in mind in our negotiations. Now, as a definite contingency and as a condition of sale, if one is to be made, there will be a distinct understanding that the services which we are giving to these isolated areas will be continued by the purchaser.

maintopic: ANNOUNCEMENT OF APPOINTMENT OF THE CHIEF JUSTICE OF CANADA, THE SPEAKER OF THE SENATE, THE SPEAKER OF THE HOUSE OF COMMONS AND THE LEADER OF THE OPPOSITION
speechtext: Will there be any provision for a similar service to new settlements, or will this protection be restricted to those settlements where there are already telephone lines?

maintopic: ANNOUNCEMENT OF APPOINTMENT OF THE CHIEF JUSTICE OF CANADA, THE SPEAKER OF THE SENATE, THE SPEAKER OF THE HOUSE OF COMMONS AND THE LEADER OF THE OPPOSITION
speechtext: It can have to do only with services already in existence and not with new services, because a purchaser unquestionably would not want to put himself in the position of having to provide a new service if the necessity arose. It must not be forgotten that while some of these services will be profitable to any purchaser, other parts unquestionably will be unprofitable.

maintopic: ANNOUNCEMENT OF APPOINTMENT OF THE CHIEF JUSTICE OF CANADA, THE SPEAKER OF THE SENATE, THE SPEAKER OF THE HOUSE OF COMMONS AND THE LEADER OF THE OPPOSITION
speechtext: Then the position is that probably there will be no telephone service for people moving into districts not now occupied?

maintopic: ANNOUNCEMENT OF APPOINTMENT OF THE CHIEF JUSTICE OF CANADA, THE SPEAKER OF THE SENATE, THE SPEAKER OF THE HOUSE OF COMMONS AND THE LEADER OF THE OPPOSITION
speechtext: In the negotiations, and in any sale which would take place, the answer would be no. But there will be the same position vis-a-vis those people and the board of transport commissioners and the Department of Transport as exists today.

maintopic: ANNOUNCEMENT OF APPOINTMENT OF THE CHIEF JUSTICE OF CANADA, THE SPEAKER OF THE SENATE, THE SPEAKER OF THE HOUSE OF COMMONS AND THE LEADER OF THE OPPOSITION
speechtext: But the people cannot compel the British Columbia Telephone Company to give a telephone service?

maintopic: ANNOUNCEMENT OF APPOINTMENT OF THE CHIEF JUSTICE OF CANADA, THE SPEAKER OF THE SENATE, THE SPEAKER OF THE HOUSE OF COMMONS AND THE LEADER OF THE OPPOSITION
speechtext: No, but there will be an opportunity for them to apply to the board of transport commissioners for facilities, and unquestionably representations will be made to us for facilities in isolated areas.

maintopic: ANNOUNCEMENT OF APPOINTMENT OF THE CHIEF JUSTICE OF CANADA, THE SPEAKER OF THE SENATE, THE SPEAKER OF THE HOUSE OF COMMONS AND THE LEADER OF THE OPPOSITION
speechtext: But has the board of transport commissioners the power to make the British Columbia Telephone Company instal a telephone system in a district?

maintopic: ANNOUNCEMENT OF APPOINTMENT OF THE CHIEF JUSTICE OF CANADA, THE SPEAKER OF THE SENATE, THE SPEAKER OF THE HOUSE OF COMMONS AND THE LEADER OF THE OPPOSITION
speechtext:
It would depend upon
whether or not the conditions existing under the Railway Act, such as public convenience and necessity, obtain. If they did, then I think the British Columbia Telephone Company would have to provide it.

maintopic: ANNOUNCEMENT OF APPOINTMENT OF THE CHIEF JUSTICE OF CANADA, THE SPEAKER OF THE SENATE, THE SPEAKER OF THE HOUSE OF COMMONS AND THE LEADER OF THE OPPOSITION
speechtext: I think the minister should check that with his officials. I may be wrong, but it has always been my understanding that you could not force the British Columbia Telephone Company to instal a telephone service.

maintopic: ANNOUNCEMENT OF APPOINTMENT OF THE CHIEF JUSTICE OF CANADA, THE SPEAKER OF THE SENATE, THE SPEAKER OF THE HOUSE OF COMMONS AND THE LEADER OF THE OPPOSITION
speechtext: I was under the impression they could; but I shall look it up.

maintopic: ANNOUNCEMENT OF APPOINTMENT OF THE CHIEF JUSTICE OF CANADA, THE SPEAKER OF THE SENATE, THE SPEAKER OF THE HOUSE OF COMMONS AND THE LEADER OF THE OPPOSITION
speechtext: May I ask a question about the British Columbia Telephone Company?

maintopic: ANNOUNCEMENT OF APPOINTMENT OF THE CHIEF JUSTICE OF CANADA, THE SPEAKER OF THE SENATE, THE SPEAKER OF THE HOUSE OF COMMONS AND THE LEADER OF THE OPPOSITION
speechtext: There have been several questions already.

maintopic: ANNOUNCEMENT OF APPOINTMENT OF THE CHIEF JUSTICE OF CANADA, THE SPEAKER OF THE SENATE, THE SPEAKER OF THE HOUSE OF COMMONS AND THE LEADER OF THE OPPOSITION
speechtext: I was detained, and have just come into the house. It has been brought to my attention that negotiations are going on between the federal government and the British Columbia Telephone Company for the purchase of the government telephone system in British Columbia. I would ask the minister to tell me if that is correct. Also, one correspondent suggested that the government was going to sell the whole system for one dollar. What is the information on these points?

maintopic: ANNOUNCEMENT OF APPOINTMENT OF THE CHIEF JUSTICE OF CANADA, THE SPEAKER OF THE SENATE, THE SPEAKER OF THE HOUSE OF COMMONS AND THE LEADER OF THE OPPOSITION
speechtext: The answer to the first question is yes, and to the second question it is definitely no.

Item agreed to.
Civil aviation division-
494. Control of civil aviation, including the administration of the Aeronautics Act and regulations issued thereunder, $886,506.
68108-330i
Supply-Transport

maintopic: ANNOUNCEMENT OF APPOINTMENT OF THE CHIEF JUSTICE OF CANADA, THE SPEAKER OF THE SENATE, THE SPEAKER OF THE HOUSE OF COMMONS AND THE LEADER OF THE OPPOSITION
speechtext:
I should like to ask a question regarding the restaurants operated at the various airports throughout the country. Are these restaurants administered by the department, or are they leased as concessions to others? I ask the question because some of them are not managed very well or in a way which would measure up to the degree of dignity commensurate with the general standards of Trans-Canada Air Lines. I shall not name the one or two I have in mind because it might not be fair, and might be embarrassing for those managing the restaurants in question.
However, I cannot help thinking that people flying to Canada and entering by way of these airports, and who use the restaurant facilities, cannot be favourably impressed. The fact of the matter is that some of these places are not clean. If they are leased under a concession I should think the department would carry out some sort of inspection.

maintopic: ANNOUNCEMENT OF APPOINTMENT OF THE CHIEF JUSTICE OF CANADA, THE SPEAKER OF THE SENATE, THE SPEAKER OF THE HOUSE OF COMMONS AND THE LEADER OF THE OPPOSITION
speechtext:
The Department of Transport does not operate any of the restaurants. We did at one time, but we were most anxious to get out of the business because the operations were unprofitable. Concessions are let by tender at each airport requiring restaurant service. Today we make a fairly good profit from them.
I think of Gander, about which there has been some discussion today. I have been there perhaps as often as at any other airport of Canada. I think the restaurant there is operated in a most efficient manner. At any time I was there I found that the meals were good. I believe the same thing can be said about Malton airport.
The point my hon. friend brings to my attention has been brought to my attention before. I think it arises because of unforeseen circumstances where many flights come in at the same time and there is a great deal of congestion in the restaurant. It is sometimes difficult for the employees to deal with the public as efficiently or in as cleanly a manner as they normally would. There is public inspection of all these restaurants, which are under the direct supervision of a manager as well as being under the airport manager. If my hon. friend has any particular restaurant in mind I shall be glad to bring it to the attention of those responsible.

maintopic: ANNOUNCEMENT OF APPOINTMENT OF THE CHIEF JUSTICE OF CANADA, THE SPEAKER OF THE SENATE, THE SPEAKER OF THE HOUSE OF COMMONS AND THE LEADER OF THE OPPOSITION
speechtext:
I must say that from coast to coast the air facilities are inadequate, and this would apply to every airport from Vancouver right through, Calgary, Malton, Winnipeg and all these various places. There are not sufficient facilities to handle the people who travel by air. We

Supply-Transport
might as well realize that we are in an air age and more room is required. Even at Dorval you find conditions very crowded, with inadequate facilities to handle the great number of people who are constantly passing through.

maintopic: ANNOUNCEMENT OF APPOINTMENT OF THE CHIEF JUSTICE OF CANADA, THE SPEAKER OF THE SENATE, THE SPEAKER OF THE HOUSE OF COMMONS AND THE LEADER OF THE OPPOSITION
speechtext: I do not want to labour this point, and I shall be glad to submit what I have in mind to the minister. It is not altogether a matter of congestion, it is a question of cleanliness and what people get to eat. When you go in to eat in a restaurant downtown and do not like it you can go to the one across the street or in some other place. But you cannot do that at an airport because these places are five, ten, twenty or twenty-five miles out of town. I do believe these places should reflect something of what we expect T.C.A. to be. T.C.A. gives very good service; the meals on the planes are lovely and there is no better way to travel, but when you go into an airport restaurant and find some girl dressed in a white smock smeared from head to foot and you look around and find they are all the same, you begin to wonder what country you have arrived in. That is what I had in mind, and perhaps that word will be passed along.

maintopic: ANNOUNCEMENT OF APPOINTMENT OF THE CHIEF JUSTICE OF CANADA, THE SPEAKER OF THE SENATE, THE SPEAKER OF THE HOUSE OF COMMONS AND THE LEADER OF THE OPPOSITION
speechtext: I think that is a "Socred" smear. No one has travelled more across this country from north to south and east to west than I, and I have never met a waitress or a person serving in our airports who was not courteous, kindly and immaculate in her starched garments.

maintopic: ANNOUNCEMENT OF APPOINTMENT OF THE CHIEF JUSTICE OF CANADA, THE SPEAKER OF THE SENATE, THE SPEAKER OF THE HOUSE OF COMMONS AND THE LEADER OF THE OPPOSITION
speechtext: The hon. member for Cariboo has been making political speeches in this house for the last few days and smearing everybody else. What I am saying has nothing to do with Social Credit or with Social Credit smears. I paid the minister the honour of saying that I was not going to indicate which one or two I had in mind because I did not want to embarrass anyone. But my hon. friend from Cariboo jumps up and says it is a Social Credit smear. He had better read some of the papers from British Columbia that are coming into the reading room and learn a little about some Liberal smears.

maintopic: ANNOUNCEMENT OF APPOINTMENT OF THE CHIEF JUSTICE OF CANADA, THE SPEAKER OF THE SENATE, THE SPEAKER OF THE HOUSE OF COMMONS AND THE LEADER OF THE OPPOSITION
speechtext:
I shall take up a lance in defence of these beautiful young ladies any afternoon. They serve us who travel and who are sometimes irritable and wanting this and that right away. The fact is that there are not sufficient facilities at these various air terminals. T.C.A. is giving a wonderful service, as is C.P.A. and the other lines. We should remember we are in

the air age. We are not in the horse and buggy age; we are not even in the autobus age; we are in the air age, and we should enlarge and improve these facilities for the service of our own people and those who want to come to our shores.

maintopic: ANNOUNCEMENT OF APPOINTMENT OF THE CHIEF JUSTICE OF CANADA, THE SPEAKER OF THE SENATE, THE SPEAKER OF THE HOUSE OF COMMONS AND THE LEADER OF THE OPPOSITION
speechtext: When I butt in between Macleod and Cariboo I wonder where I am going to end.

maintopic: ANNOUNCEMENT OF APPOINTMENT OF THE CHIEF JUSTICE OF CANADA, THE SPEAKER OF THE SENATE, THE SPEAKER OF THE HOUSE OF COMMONS AND THE LEADER OF THE OPPOSITION
speechtext: Gander.

maintopic: ANNOUNCEMENT OF APPOINTMENT OF THE CHIEF JUSTICE OF CANADA, THE SPEAKER OF THE SENATE, THE SPEAKER OF THE HOUSE OF COMMONS AND THE LEADER OF THE OPPOSITION
speechtext:
I want to pay tribute to Trans-Canada service because it is grand so far as I am concerned. I want to ask the minister two questions. I did not think he answered the first one fully this morning. I was inquiring about new commercial routes for Trans-Canada in the United States. I sent over a newspaper clipping about what the minister is reputed to have said in connection with what was going to happen. I should like to know what the facts are; but if he feels he should not state it publicly, that is all right.
The next matter is the need for adequate runways at Gander which would be in service during the spring break-up. These should be provided at once or we are going to lose the United States air services. I am not speaking now from the standpoint of Newfoundland only, and I do not think I could do this because there are so many people using air services today, and these runways should be properly constructed. The minister knows what I have in mind because I have spoken to him about it before. There should be three 6,000-foot runways for allweather service and able to operate in spring time. The minister will know what I am talking about and I hope he will give consideration to this.
The one question I did want him to answer was about the new commercial air routes.

maintopic: ANNOUNCEMENT OF APPOINTMENT OF THE CHIEF JUSTICE OF CANADA, THE SPEAKER OF THE SENATE, THE SPEAKER OF THE HOUSE OF COMMONS AND THE LEADER OF THE OPPOSITION
speechtext:
That is the one my hon. friend did not ask, and for that reason I did not give an answer. I must say that he did send me over a clipping, but apparently he forgot to ask the question. This has to do with the negotiation of the bilateral agreement with the United States. We indicated some time ago to the United States government through their civil aeronautics board that we thought the time had arrived for a renegotiation of the bilateral agreement. In fact we think this should be done more often than every four years. It is our hope that it will be possible for us to get the additional routes we would like as amendments to the bilateral agreement, and we would be ready to listen to any representations which they would care to make. We

have not fixed the date, but we shall be meeting soon.
With regard to the second matter raised by the hon. member, he may rest assured that we in the department consider Gander a very important airport. That is evidenced by the fact that we built a large runway last year and are to build one this year. There is an item in the estimates for that purpose, together with other substantial amounts for meteorological services. In fact there was something like $2 million for Gander in the estimates this year.

speakerposition: Whip of the Co-operative Commonwealth Federation
maintopic: ANNOUNCEMENT OF APPOINTMENT OF THE CHIEF JUSTICE OF CANADA, THE SPEAKER OF THE SENATE, THE SPEAKER OF THE HOUSE OF COMMONS AND THE LEADER OF THE OPPOSITION
speechtext: I take it from what the minister has said that these discussions with the United States will relate only to additional routes. Is it the case that we already grant each other all the freedoms under international civil aviation?

maintopic: ANNOUNCEMENT OF APPOINTMENT OF THE CHIEF JUSTICE OF CANADA, THE SPEAKER OF THE SENATE, THE SPEAKER OF THE HOUSE OF COMMONS AND THE LEADER OF THE OPPOSITION
speechtext: Not necessarily. It depends on what each country wants. When we met last there were certain things that we were very anxious to get. Those were the transborder routes. As it is now we would like to get additional trans-border routes. We have in mind two facilities for C.P.A. on the west coast, and additional facilities for Trans-Canada Air Lines in eastern Canada via the United States. Those and other matters, all having to do with air routes, will be taken up when the discussions are started.

Item agreed to.
495. Civil aviation services, $9,138,575.

maintopic: ANNOUNCEMENT OF APPOINTMENT OF THE CHIEF JUSTICE OF CANADA, THE SPEAKER OF THE SENATE, THE SPEAKER OF THE HOUSE OF COMMONS AND THE LEADER OF THE OPPOSITION
speechtext: For some years negotiations have been under way between the Minister of Transport and the city of Vancouver concerning the possibility of the government taking over the Vancouver airport. The last word I had was that the minister had offered to pay $900,000 and the city was asking $1,276,000. I believe there have been negotiations since these figures were last made public. Can the minister bring us up to date on that question?

maintopic: ANNOUNCEMENT OF APPOINTMENT OF THE CHIEF JUSTICE OF CANADA, THE SPEAKER OF THE SENATE, THE SPEAKER OF THE HOUSE OF COMMONS AND THE LEADER OF THE OPPOSITION
speechtext:
As far as I can recollect, the last time I had any discussions with the airport committee of the city of Vancouver it was simply to restate the position. The city of Vancouver presented a proposal to us which we were unable to accept. In fact the discussions I had with the mayor and with, I think, Alderman Cornett and perhaps two or three other aldermen, were very friendly and to the point that we in the department would much prefer if they would operate the airport. In fact wherever possible we want to see municipalities such as Vancouver operate airports. It is now not so much a question of arriving at an amount as of hoping that the
Supply-Transport
city will continue its operation. My recollection is that with that in mind I instructed our officers to prepare a lease or an agreement with the municipality for a continuation of the operation of the airport by the municipality. Since then I have received word that the mayor wanted to come down and discuss the matter with me, but beyond that I can say no more.

maintopic: ANNOUNCEMENT OF APPOINTMENT OF THE CHIEF JUSTICE OF CANADA, THE SPEAKER OF THE SENATE, THE SPEAKER OF THE HOUSE OF COMMONS AND THE LEADER OF THE OPPOSITION
speechtext: Is it not a fact that the city is not in a position to construct the improvements that are required for an airport of that size?

maintopic: ANNOUNCEMENT OF APPOINTMENT OF THE CHIEF JUSTICE OF CANADA, THE SPEAKER OF THE SENATE, THE SPEAKER OF THE HOUSE OF COMMONS AND THE LEADER OF THE OPPOSITION
speechtext: That would have nothing to do with the operation of the airport, in any event.

maintopic: ANNOUNCEMENT OF APPOINTMENT OF THE CHIEF JUSTICE OF CANADA, THE SPEAKER OF THE SENATE, THE SPEAKER OF THE HOUSE OF COMMONS AND THE LEADER OF THE OPPOSITION
speechtext:
I find that in the year 1952 that airport recorded 202,311 aircraft movements, which was 70,000 more than its nearest rival, the airport at Edmonton, which shows what a big undertaking it is. Just a few months ago Grant McConachie, who is the president of Canadian Pacific Air Lines, when speaking in Vancouver, pointed out that there was need for great developments in that airport. He said he thought there would be a direct service over the pole from Vancouver to Europe. Apparently some Swedish line has already flown that route from the west coast of the United States. Here is what he said with regard to the Vancouver airport:
Vancouver is destined to become the Canadian "skygate to the world", the air portal to Australia, Asia, South America, and Europe, he said.
"But, if Vancouver is to retain its rightful place in the global airlanes of tomorrow, this airport must be developed to the highest standards of any in the world. I believe this is properly the responsibility of the federal government, rather than the local taxpayer."
Is it not a fact that that statement by Grant McConachie is correct? The airport is now doing so much business and is so important that it simply cannot be expected that the Vancouver taxpayers can handle it. I believe Dorval is a dominion airport, and I think that is also true of Malton. I am afraid it is impossible to expect the local taxpayers to keep that airport developed to the degree which the traffic warrants. Is that not the actual situation?

maintopic: ANNOUNCEMENT OF APPOINTMENT OF THE CHIEF JUSTICE OF CANADA, THE SPEAKER OF THE SENATE, THE SPEAKER OF THE HOUSE OF COMMONS AND THE LEADER OF THE OPPOSITION
speechtext: No.

maintopic: ANNOUNCEMENT OF APPOINTMENT OF THE CHIEF JUSTICE OF CANADA, THE SPEAKER OF THE SENATE, THE SPEAKER OF THE HOUSE OF COMMONS AND THE LEADER OF THE OPPOSITION
speechtext:
How long can this present system carry on? I do not believe it can carry on indefinitely, and I would hope that the minister would reopen negotiations with the mayor if and when he comes here. I hope it will be possible for the two parties to get together. They were not very far apart before, and it does seem a great shame that they cannot reach an agreement with regard to the dominion taking over the airport.

Supply-Transport

maintopic: ANNOUNCEMENT OF APPOINTMENT OF THE CHIEF JUSTICE OF CANADA, THE SPEAKER OF THE SENATE, THE SPEAKER OF THE HOUSE OF COMMONS AND THE LEADER OF THE OPPOSITION
speechtext:
Let me tell my hon. friend right away that the taxpayer of the city of Vancouver is not going to be affected in any way by this deal. Whether we take it over or whether it is operated by the municipality of Vancouver will not affect the facilities in so far as the airport itself is concerned.
My hon. friend referred to the statement made by the president of C.P.A., Grant McConachie, with which I would not disagree. What he says is quite true. The airport is right in the centre of the air routes of the world and occupies on the west coast perhaps the same position Gander occupies on the east coast; but let it not be forgotten that if the municipality of Vancouver operates it, it is not going to suffer in any way. In any event, it is the Department of Transport that will provide many of the facilities. As it is now, we built an airway last year while it was being operated by the city of Vancouver. We have in mind, in conjunction with the municipal authorities, the question of a new terminal building, and when facilities are required we may ask the municipality to make some contribution because of the capital that has already been invested by the municipality. But let me assure my hon. friend that no facilities will be neglected at Vancouver because this deal does not go through.

maintopic: ANNOUNCEMENT OF APPOINTMENT OF THE CHIEF JUSTICE OF CANADA, THE SPEAKER OF THE SENATE, THE SPEAKER OF THE HOUSE OF COMMONS AND THE LEADER OF THE OPPOSITION
speechtext: Is the minister willing to negotiate further with the mayor?

maintopic: ANNOUNCEMENT OF APPOINTMENT OF THE CHIEF JUSTICE OF CANADA, THE SPEAKER OF THE SENATE, THE SPEAKER OF THE HOUSE OF COMMONS AND THE LEADER OF THE OPPOSITION
speechtext: I never close the door on anything, and if the mayor wants to come down with his committee and discuss matters with me I shall be glad to see him.

maintopic: ANNOUNCEMENT OF APPOINTMENT OF THE CHIEF JUSTICE OF CANADA, THE SPEAKER OF THE SENATE, THE SPEAKER OF THE HOUSE OF COMMONS AND THE LEADER OF THE OPPOSITION
speechtext:
After listening to the discussion one would think that this airport of Vancouver was dealing with an unfriendly foreign power. Everybody knows that the airport at Vancouver is an international airport. It was made so because of its geographical position, not because of any virtues in Vancouver. Those of us who reside in the interior and who must use the air lines to get into Vancouver have this happen to us. We get on the plane at Fort St. John and after two or three hours we are at the international airport at Vancouver. By using a lot of intelligence we get a taxicab to go into town. Having got a taxicab to proceed to the city of Vancouver, the third city of our great Canada, we go two or three miles and we come to a little bridge such as you might see in the backwoods country of Kaza-bazua or up in the north woods. There is a barrier you must not pass. Some little steamboat has to go under the Marpole bridge with a couple of logs behind it. After breaking

your neck and after paying your good money to come from Fort St. John to Vancouver you have to stay there and wait until this boat with these few logs gets through, and after two or three hours you get into Vancouver.
It is a confirmation of what I said a few moments ago, that we are living in an air age but the city of Vancouver is back to the horse and buggy days. There is no question about it. If the Department of Transport ever offered the city of Vancouver one dollar for that airport, why, the city of Vancouver should accept it and say: "It is splendid."
It is a magnificent airport, situated as they have said at a very strategic place. Mr. McConachie, one of our greatest men in air traffic today, has developed plans for travel from the new international airport there to Australia, New Zealand, South America, Asia -that is to Japan and China-and so forth. As the minister has said, he has planned to go over the pole to Europe.
Why, if the people of Vancouver would only open their eyes they would realize that they are in a great age of expansion, in the air age. They would, of course, turn that airport over to the Department of Transport for $1 and good intentions; and I am sure the government of Canada would build a bridge over the Marpole bottleneck or blockade, or whatever you wish to call it, which would enable people from all over the world to travel quickly into one of the most beautiful cities in the world today, the great city of Vancouver.
As a man from the hinterland I will tell you that the thing is wrapped up in a whole lot of parish politics, this and that, Social Credit and so forth. The destiny of that great city has narrowed down into the little bottleneck of the Marpole bridge where a village constable comes out and says: "Well, after a while you can pass"; and after a while you can pass. As I say, this is an age of speed and air travel and that sort of thing, but I think it is silly when we go to so much expense to make speed to get somewhere and, after we get there, sit down, light a cigarette, drink some coffee and after two or three hours a taxicab gets you into town.

maintopic: ANNOUNCEMENT OF APPOINTMENT OF THE CHIEF JUSTICE OF CANADA, THE SPEAKER OF THE SENATE, THE SPEAKER OF THE HOUSE OF COMMONS AND THE LEADER OF THE OPPOSITION
speechtext:
I cannot let the hon. member for Cariboo get away with all those remarks. The citizens of Vancouver have a good many hundreds of thousands of dollars invested in the airport, and the Marpole bridge is not their responsibility. That bridge is between Vancouver city and another municipality. For many years there has been an attempt

to reach agreement among the city, the province and the dominion for the construction of a new bridge. The city council has offered to put any money they get from the airport into this new bridge. I do not know which of the senior governments is to blame for the lack of action, but certainly it is not the council of the city of Vancouver. I believe the dominion government and the provincial government must share the responsibility for failure to have a proper bridge built.

maintopic: ANNOUNCEMENT OF APPOINTMENT OF THE CHIEF JUSTICE OF CANADA, THE SPEAKER OF THE SENATE, THE SPEAKER OF THE HOUSE OF COMMONS AND THE LEADER OF THE OPPOSITION
speechtext: If Mr. Laing is elected premier of British Columbia this whole thing will be resolved.

maintopic: ANNOUNCEMENT OF APPOINTMENT OF THE CHIEF JUSTICE OF CANADA, THE SPEAKER OF THE SENATE, THE SPEAKER OF THE HOUSE OF COMMONS AND THE LEADER OF THE OPPOSITION
speechtext:
I just want to make this statment. If my hon. friend wants to charge the federal government with responsibility I must say to him that the Department of Transport has no responsibility as far as the Marpole bridge is concerned, and I think he knows that. There has been some attempt to charge this department with responsibility for construction of the bridge, but I think it is admitted on all sides that it has not that responsibility. The Department of Transport does not build bridges of this kind.
As far as blame for lack of construction is concerned, I do not think it is up to the federal government to take the initiative. I do not know what is in the mind of the municipality of the city of Vancouver but, as I said to my hon. friend, if they have any proposition to put to me I shall be glad to listen to it. When it was put to me it was not on that basis; it was on the basis of an out and out sale.

maintopic: ANNOUNCEMENT OF APPOINTMENT OF THE CHIEF JUSTICE OF CANADA, THE SPEAKER OF THE SENATE, THE SPEAKER OF THE HOUSE OF COMMONS AND THE LEADER OF THE OPPOSITION
speechtext: I think that is the understanding, that any money paid by the dominion would be used to help construct the bridge.

maintopic: ANNOUNCEMENT OF APPOINTMENT OF THE CHIEF JUSTICE OF CANADA, THE SPEAKER OF THE SENATE, THE SPEAKER OF THE HOUSE OF COMMONS AND THE LEADER OF THE OPPOSITION
speechtext: I was not aware of that.

maintopic: ANNOUNCEMENT OF APPOINTMENT OF THE CHIEF JUSTICE OF CANADA, THE SPEAKER OF THE SENATE, THE SPEAKER OF THE HOUSE OF COMMONS AND THE LEADER OF THE OPPOSITION
speechtext: This may not be the department responsible for helping to construct the bridge but other ministers, notably the Minister of Trade and Commerce, have been involved in these negotiations. It is just too bad that no progress has been made.

maintopic: ANNOUNCEMENT OF APPOINTMENT OF THE CHIEF JUSTICE OF CANADA, THE SPEAKER OF THE SENATE, THE SPEAKER OF THE HOUSE OF COMMONS AND THE LEADER OF THE OPPOSITION
speechtext: Probably I am not right in putting my question here, and the item may have come up before I arrived. However, I would like to ask the minister on this item, civil aviation, whether he has anything further to report with reference to the airport at Charlottetown, Prince Edward Island?

maintopic: ANNOUNCEMENT OF APPOINTMENT OF THE CHIEF JUSTICE OF CANADA, THE SPEAKER OF THE SENATE, THE SPEAKER OF THE HOUSE OF COMMONS AND THE LEADER OF THE OPPOSITION
speechtext:
There is an item in the estimates for the extension of the runway at Charlottetown; but it is on the distinct understanding that the municipality will operate the airport.
Supply-Transport

maintopic: ANNOUNCEMENT OF APPOINTMENT OF THE CHIEF JUSTICE OF CANADA, THE SPEAKER OF THE SENATE, THE SPEAKER OF THE HOUSE OF COMMONS AND THE LEADER OF THE OPPOSITION
speechtext:
This is an item for over $9 million. If we look back to the preceding page we see an item for $15 million for telecommunications and $6 million for meteorological services. If we are allowed to cast our eyes forward a couple of items we find another item of $9 million for construction.
I get almost dizzy over the apparent complexity of the organization. In item 494 we have control of civil aviation, and at page 546 I find that we have a controller of civil aviation. Then we come to the item which is called "civil aviation services", and I read at page 548 that we have a superintendent of airways. A little later we come to construction and at page 553 I find that we have a superintendent of construction, air services.
Altogether, Mr. Chairman, we are considering items amounting to between $40 and $50 million, and I would ask the minister who has charge of all of this. As I look at these three services-control of civil aviation, control of civil aviation services, and construction services, judging from the relation of their salaries those at the head are evidently rated very much at the same level. These are tremendously large amounts, and I wish the minister would indicate what over-all supervision there is. Are these three officials working more or less on their own, keeping in touch with each other as best they may? What is the division of authority between them, and to whom do they report? Who is responsible for seeing that there is no overlapping in each of these services? I shall not take time to list them but there are scores, probably hundreds of employees in some cases. It is a tremendous undertaking in which the people of Canada are spending well on toward $50 million a year.
I want to add that the air transport board comes in here. Would the minister just indicate in a general way who is at the head of this organization? Who is responsible? Who controls these various departments and assumes responsibility to the minister- because after all he has twenty other things to do? Who assumes responsibility to him that these things are all co-ordinated, that there is no overlapping, and that the whole matter runs smoothly and efficiently.

maintopic: ANNOUNCEMENT OF APPOINTMENT OF THE CHIEF JUSTICE OF CANADA, THE SPEAKER OF THE SENATE, THE SPEAKER OF THE HOUSE OF COMMONS AND THE LEADER OF THE OPPOSITION
speechtext:
Mr. Chairman, the civil aviation branch of the Department of Transport is divided under three headings. There are first the meteorological services, next the telecommunications services, and third the civil aviation. Each of the three has a controller, and the over-all director is the

Supply-Transport
director of air services. The director of air services is responsible for the control of telecommunications, for the control of civil aviation and for the control of meteorological services. Each division spends a tremendous amount of money because airport, airways and air route facilities cost a great deal of money. The radio services in particular are extremely expensive. Radio facilities and the necessary air routes are matters of considerable expense. The matter of taking weather observations is a branch of the department under the controller of meteorological services. The three controllers report to the director of air services who happens to be Air Vice Marshal Cowley, a very old and experienced and trusted officer of the department.
Again, those three divisions are broken down into various other divisions such as air regulations, airways and airports, aeronautical engineering, construction and civil engineering. The vote with which we are concerned at the moment is one which has to do with construction, and which has to do with the building of airports, airstrips, terminal buildings and the like from one end of the country to the other. It is for that reason that the amount is so large. When one considers that to build an airstrip capable of taking the most modern aircraft it costs, roughly speaking, anywhere from three-quarters of a million to a million dollars, one realizes at once that you cannot go very far with a vote of $9 million. Those are the main divisions of the department in so far as the civil aviation branch is concerned.
Now, the hon. member asked something about the air transport board. The air transport board is that body which deals with the licensing of air routes. It is represented by the chairman, who is Mr. John R. Baldwin, and it has two functions, one a regulatory function and the other an advisory function. The duties of this body are set out in the Aeronautics Act. Under that act one will find that the air transport board has an advisory responsibility to the minister, and in some cases to the government. It is the body that grants licences for all the air lines, either commercial, passenger or cargo. I could go on with perhaps ten or fifteen other different categories of licences.

maintopic: ANNOUNCEMENT OF APPOINTMENT OF THE CHIEF JUSTICE OF CANADA, THE SPEAKER OF THE SENATE, THE SPEAKER OF THE HOUSE OF COMMONS AND THE LEADER OF THE OPPOSITION
speechtext: Would the minister say a word about international civil aviation?

maintopic: ANNOUNCEMENT OF APPOINTMENT OF THE CHIEF JUSTICE OF CANADA, THE SPEAKER OF THE SENATE, THE SPEAKER OF THE HOUSE OF COMMONS AND THE LEADER OF THE OPPOSITION
speechtext:
The air transport board makes advisory recommendations to the governor in council in connection with international service. For instance, there have been negotiations between Canadian Pacific Air Lines

and the government of Mexico for an air route along the west coast, from Vancouver through San Francisco and on into Mexico. Canadian Pacific Air Lines are anxious to operate there. We must give something in return for that service. The air transport board is the body that will carry on negotiations on behalf of the government with Mexico to ascertain, first of all, if it is possible to arrange for alternate routes on the west coast. Trans-Canada Air Lines is interested also in going into Mexico on the east coast, and it might be necessary to make certain concessions to the government of Mexico so they may operate an air line into eastern Canada, either through Montreal or Toronto.
In so far as the international aspect of this matter is concerned, the air transport board will not only advise the government as to whether or not it is to the advantage of Canada to grant reciprocal rights in exchange for certain rights in Mexico, but will carry on negotiations on behalf of the government, together with representatives of the Department of External Affairs.

maintopic: ANNOUNCEMENT OF APPOINTMENT OF THE CHIEF JUSTICE OF CANADA, THE SPEAKER OF THE SENATE, THE SPEAKER OF THE HOUSE OF COMMONS AND THE LEADER OF THE OPPOSITION
speechtext:
My understanding is that the heads of these three departments report to Air Vice Marshal
Cowley?

maintopic: ANNOUNCEMENT OF APPOINTMENT OF THE CHIEF JUSTICE OF CANADA, THE SPEAKER OF THE SENATE, THE SPEAKER OF THE HOUSE OF COMMONS AND THE LEADER OF THE OPPOSITION
speechtext: That is right.

maintopic: ANNOUNCEMENT OF APPOINTMENT OF THE CHIEF JUSTICE OF CANADA, THE SPEAKER OF THE SENATE, THE SPEAKER OF THE HOUSE OF COMMONS AND THE LEADER OF THE OPPOSITION
speechtext:
He is in
control, co-ordinating and regulating the whole thing and reporting to the minister?

maintopic: ANNOUNCEMENT OF APPOINTMENT OF THE CHIEF JUSTICE OF CANADA, THE SPEAKER OF THE SENATE, THE SPEAKER OF THE HOUSE OF COMMONS AND THE LEADER OF THE OPPOSITION
speechtext: That is right.

maintopic: ANNOUNCEMENT OF APPOINTMENT OF THE CHIEF JUSTICE OF CANADA, THE SPEAKER OF THE SENATE, THE SPEAKER OF THE HOUSE OF COMMONS AND THE LEADER OF THE OPPOSITION
speechtext:
Under date of May 7 there is a press release from the Royal Canadian Air Force which relates to Torbay airport in Newfoundland. It reads:
Department of Transport meteorologists and telecommunications operators are remaining at Torbay to carry out essential duties, and the change-over allows for continuation of limited commercial operations from the station.
What does that mean?

maintopic: ANNOUNCEMENT OF APPOINTMENT OF THE CHIEF JUSTICE OF CANADA, THE SPEAKER OF THE SENATE, THE SPEAKER OF THE HOUSE OF COMMONS AND THE LEADER OF THE OPPOSITION
speechtext: This is a transfer of Torbay to the United States air force because United States defence forces-

maintopic: ANNOUNCEMENT OF APPOINTMENT OF THE CHIEF JUSTICE OF CANADA, THE SPEAKER OF THE SENATE, THE SPEAKER OF THE HOUSE OF COMMONS AND THE LEADER OF THE OPPOSITION
speechtext: I am afraid that is not so.

maintopic: ANNOUNCEMENT OF APPOINTMENT OF THE CHIEF JUSTICE OF CANADA, THE SPEAKER OF THE SENATE, THE SPEAKER OF THE HOUSE OF COMMONS AND THE LEADER OF THE OPPOSITION
speechtext: I am afraid I have misinterpreted this. It is a transfer by the United States air force to the R.C.A.F. because of the interest the R.C.A.F. have in Torbay.

maintopic: ANNOUNCEMENT OF APPOINTMENT OF THE CHIEF JUSTICE OF CANADA, THE SPEAKER OF THE SENATE, THE SPEAKER OF THE HOUSE OF COMMONS AND THE LEADER OF THE OPPOSITION
speechtext: It cannot be a transfer from the United States.

maintopic: ANNOUNCEMENT OF APPOINTMENT OF THE CHIEF JUSTICE OF CANADA, THE SPEAKER OF THE SENATE, THE SPEAKER OF THE HOUSE OF COMMONS AND THE LEADER OF THE OPPOSITION
speechtext: I am afraid the hon. member had better repeat his question. I was not able to follow him.

maintopic: ANNOUNCEMENT OF APPOINTMENT OF THE CHIEF JUSTICE OF CANADA, THE SPEAKER OF THE SENATE, THE SPEAKER OF THE HOUSE OF COMMONS AND THE LEADER OF THE OPPOSITION
speechtext:
I shall read this again, if you do not mind. It is a press release from defence headquarters, and the last paragraph reads:
Department of Transport meteorologists and telecommunications operators are remaining at Torbay to carry out essential duties, and the change-over allows for continuation of limited commercial operations from the station.
What does that mean? That is all I asked the minister.

maintopic: ANNOUNCEMENT OF APPOINTMENT OF THE CHIEF JUSTICE OF CANADA, THE SPEAKER OF THE SENATE, THE SPEAKER OF THE HOUSE OF COMMONS AND THE LEADER OF THE OPPOSITION
speechtext: I am informed that we are transferring our interests in the airport to the R.C.A.F., but we are maintaining facilities for civil aviation at Torbay.

maintopic: ANNOUNCEMENT OF APPOINTMENT OF THE CHIEF JUSTICE OF CANADA, THE SPEAKER OF THE SENATE, THE SPEAKER OF THE HOUSE OF COMMONS AND THE LEADER OF THE OPPOSITION
speechtext: Will there be any diminution of the facilities so far as civil aviation is concerned?

maintopic: ANNOUNCEMENT OF APPOINTMENT OF THE CHIEF JUSTICE OF CANADA, THE SPEAKER OF THE SENATE, THE SPEAKER OF THE HOUSE OF COMMONS AND THE LEADER OF THE OPPOSITION
speechtext: Not in so far as civil aviation is concerned.

maintopic: ANNOUNCEMENT OF APPOINTMENT OF THE CHIEF JUSTICE OF CANADA, THE SPEAKER OF THE SENATE, THE SPEAKER OF THE HOUSE OF COMMONS AND THE LEADER OF THE OPPOSITION
speechtext: Has the department given any consideration to a possible route from the west coast over the pole to Europe?

maintopic: ANNOUNCEMENT OF APPOINTMENT OF THE CHIEF JUSTICE OF CANADA, THE SPEAKER OF THE SENATE, THE SPEAKER OF THE HOUSE OF COMMONS AND THE LEADER OF THE OPPOSITION
speechtext: Well, consideration has been given to it, but there has been no application for an air route. This could only have reference to long-term plans of operation, and there has been no application for a route across the pole.

Item agreed to.
Construction services-
498. Construction or acquisition of buildings, works, land and new equipment-capital, $8,919,825.

maintopic: ANNOUNCEMENT OF APPOINTMENT OF THE CHIEF JUSTICE OF CANADA, THE SPEAKER OF THE SENATE, THE SPEAKER OF THE HOUSE OF COMMONS AND THE LEADER OF THE OPPOSITION
speechtext:
When the minister made his introductory remarks on his estimates some time ago, he was good enough to mention the city of Prince Rupert. As the minister knows only too well, I could make a very long speech without repeating myself on the subject of the need for an airport at Prince Rupert. I think the minister has heard more from me than he thinks necessary, but at this point I do wish to quote two sentences from a letter on the subject by perhaps Canada's outstanding aviation expert, Mr. McConachie, president of Canadian Pacific Air Lines. In writing to the chamber of commerce of Prince Rupert on February 6 last with regard to this subject, he said:
As you know proper service to Prince Rupert cannot be provided until such time as the airport is completed, and when it is land planes will be put on from Edmonton right through to Prince Rupert. I sincerely hope your organization will continually press for this essential development.
That, I repeat, is a statement by the president of Canadian Pacific Air Lines. Attention of the house has been drawn already this evening to the report of the tragic fatality G8108-331
Supply-Transport
at Prince Rupert which would not have occurred had there not been dependence upon waterborne aircraft. Now, that is all I am going to say on the subject, except to ask the minister if he will kindly tell us what his department has in view in connection with the airport at Prince Rupert, and I mean what they have in view for 1953.

maintopic: ANNOUNCEMENT OF APPOINTMENT OF THE CHIEF JUSTICE OF CANADA, THE SPEAKER OF THE SENATE, THE SPEAKER OF THE HOUSE OF COMMONS AND THE LEADER OF THE OPPOSITION
speechtext: Mr. Chairman, there is an item in the estimates to provide for facilities and an airstrip able to take land craft. We have given consideration to three sites at Prince Rupert, all of which are costly to construct and operate. We have come to the conclusion that the site of Digby island is one that would be most economical from a long range standpoint. We have provided in the estimates a sufficient amount of money to make investigations and surveys of that type and to proceed, if the site is found to be satisfactory, with the construction of a strip on the island that will take care of the heaviest aircraft.

Item agreed to.
Civil aviation division-airways and airports- construction services-
752. Construction or acquisition of buildings, works, land and new equipment-capital-further amount required, $1,113,000.

maintopic: ANNOUNCEMENT OF APPOINTMENT OF THE CHIEF JUSTICE OF CANADA, THE SPEAKER OF THE SENATE, THE SPEAKER OF THE HOUSE OF COMMONS AND THE LEADER OF THE OPPOSITION
speechtext:
I intend to take a minute or two on this item, Mr. Chairman. For the information of the committee I might say that for centuries a small tribe of Indians lived at the junction of the Kootenay and the Columbia rivers. Then about 60 years ago two or three log huts were built near that point. In 1906 the first school was built and the village of Castlegar was established. Since that time there has been a somewhat slow development, but in the last ten years there has been such rapid development that at present Castlegar is one of the most rapidly growing municipalities in British Columbia, and with that development has come an increased demand for air service.
Four or five years ago the municipalities of Nelson, Castlegar and Kinnaird got together and undertook the construction of an airport at Castlegar on some land formerly owned by the Doukhobors. The minister's department has assisted with a grant on three separate occasions. But owing to the increased traffic and the heavier planes that are required, the airport committee, the chambers of commerce and various other groups in the constituency as well as individuals made representations to the minister for an additional grant, which is included in this item, to complete the paving

Supply-Transport
of the strips and the development of the airport so that it will accommodate the heavier planes.
The Castlegar airport committee and the people I represent have asked me to express, when this item came before the committee, their sincere appreciation of the minister's consideration of the need for further assistance. Representations were made, supported by the hon. member for Kootenay West. When the minister was convinced of the need, he recommended this grant. We are extremely pleased indeed that this grant is being made for the further development of the airport. I can assure the minister that this money will be most carefully expended and that good results will be assured from this grant.
In addition to that, I have been asked to express our appreciation to the Minister of Fisheries. He knows the airport personally. He has visited it. The airport committee discussed the situation with him, and they appreciate his support in connection with this grant. I must say, Mr. Chairman, that without any doubt the investment of this grant in the Castlegar airport will prove of great value to the people of the interior of British Columbia.

maintopic: ANNOUNCEMENT OF APPOINTMENT OF THE CHIEF JUSTICE OF CANADA, THE SPEAKER OF THE SENATE, THE SPEAKER OF THE HOUSE OF COMMONS AND THE LEADER OF THE OPPOSITION
speechtext: Before the item carries, there are about three questions I should like to ask the minister dealing with the airport at Crumlin near London, Ontario. In the estimates is there provision for increasing the length of the runways at London?

maintopic: ANNOUNCEMENT OF APPOINTMENT OF THE CHIEF JUSTICE OF CANADA, THE SPEAKER OF THE SENATE, THE SPEAKER OF THE HOUSE OF COMMONS AND THE LEADER OF THE OPPOSITION
speechtext: No.

maintopic: ANNOUNCEMENT OF APPOINTMENT OF THE CHIEF JUSTICE OF CANADA, THE SPEAKER OF THE SENATE, THE SPEAKER OF THE HOUSE OF COMMONS AND THE LEADER OF THE OPPOSITION
speechtext: Is it the duty of the minister's department to acquire land and increase the length of the runways or is it the duty of the R.C.A.F.? Both the department and the R.C.A.F. operate out of Crumlin.

maintopic: ANNOUNCEMENT OF APPOINTMENT OF THE CHIEF JUSTICE OF CANADA, THE SPEAKER OF THE SENATE, THE SPEAKER OF THE HOUSE OF COMMONS AND THE LEADER OF THE OPPOSITION
speechtext: The answer to the first question is no. The answer to the second question is that if it is an R.C.A.F. airport or if it is jointly operated by both and the land is required for defence purposes, they will ask to have an expropriation and we proceed at their request.

maintopic: ANNOUNCEMENT OF APPOINTMENT OF THE CHIEF JUSTICE OF CANADA, THE SPEAKER OF THE SENATE, THE SPEAKER OF THE HOUSE OF COMMONS AND THE LEADER OF THE OPPOSITION
speechtext: But there is no money in this vote for that purpose?

maintopic: ANNOUNCEMENT OF APPOINTMENT OF THE CHIEF JUSTICE OF CANADA, THE SPEAKER OF THE SENATE, THE SPEAKER OF THE HOUSE OF COMMONS AND THE LEADER OF THE OPPOSITION
speechtext: We have not been asked by the Department of National Defence to expropriate lands at London.

Item agreed to.
Civil aviation division-
755. To authorize the Minister of Transport to undertake to purchase, from federal government

employees, lots purchased by them in the townsite of Gander, Newfoundland, and houses and related works constructed on such lots, $1.

maintopic: ANNOUNCEMENT OF APPOINTMENT OF THE CHIEF JUSTICE OF CANADA, THE SPEAKER OF THE SENATE, THE SPEAKER OF THE HOUSE OF COMMONS AND THE LEADER OF THE OPPOSITION
speechtext: May I ask the minister to explain this item?

maintopic: ANNOUNCEMENT OF APPOINTMENT OF THE CHIEF JUSTICE OF CANADA, THE SPEAKER OF THE SENATE, THE SPEAKER OF THE HOUSE OF COMMONS AND THE LEADER OF THE OPPOSITION
speechtext: Yes. This is the item in the supplementaries. It has to do with the town-site at Gander. As the hon. member knows, Central Mortgage and Housing Corporation are building some 50 houses at the moment. We are particularly interested because of the employees of the Department of Transport there. We want our employees to own their own homes. This item of $1 is in the estimates so that if perchance some of our employees, after they have purchased their homes, are transferred to other parts of Canada, we will repurchase from them-so there will not be a loss-and sell to other employees. The reason for that $1 is this. We may not have to expend any money, but it is to have the principle recognized so in case we want to come to their assistance, it will be possible for us to do so.

maintopic: ANNOUNCEMENT OF APPOINTMENT OF THE CHIEF JUSTICE OF CANADA, THE SPEAKER OF THE SENATE, THE SPEAKER OF THE HOUSE OF COMMONS AND THE LEADER OF THE OPPOSITION
speechtext: I thank the minister for his explanation. It looked a little bit odd to me. It came down from $1,196,000. I wondered whether it would be a sweepstake ticket, to come down to a dollar.

speakerposition: Whip of the Co-operative Commonwealth Federation
maintopic: ANNOUNCEMENT OF APPOINTMENT OF THE CHIEF JUSTICE OF CANADA, THE SPEAKER OF THE SENATE, THE SPEAKER OF THE HOUSE OF COMMONS AND THE LEADER OF THE OPPOSITION
speechtext: You can do a great deal for a dollar when you want to.

Item agreed to.
Air transport board-
504.	Salaries and other expenses, including the Canadian delegation to the international civil aviation organization, $259,674.

maintopic: ANNOUNCEMENT OF APPOINTMENT OF THE CHIEF JUSTICE OF CANADA, THE SPEAKER OF THE SENATE, THE SPEAKER OF THE HOUSE OF COMMONS AND THE LEADER OF THE OPPOSITION
speechtext: I understand that some weeks ago an application was made before the air transport board in connection with an air cargo service to western Canada. Can the minister tell us what happened to that application?

maintopic: ANNOUNCEMENT OF APPOINTMENT OF THE CHIEF JUSTICE OF CANADA, THE SPEAKER OF THE SENATE, THE SPEAKER OF THE HOUSE OF COMMONS AND THE LEADER OF THE OPPOSITION
speechtext: All I can say is that Canadian Pacific Air Lines have made application to the air transport board to operate a cargo service from Montreal and/or Toronto to Vancouver via The Pas and Edmonton. That application was heard by the air transport board. Prominent counsel appeared and there were many days of hearings. As the matter stands now, no decision has been taken. It was a fairly lengthy hearing. There have been many hundreds of pages of evidence. The air transport board have not yet given me their report. Until they do so, I am not in a position to make any statement.

Item agreed to.

Air transport board-
505.	Subventions for air carriers, as detailed in the estimates, $25,000.

maintopic: ANNOUNCEMENT OF APPOINTMENT OF THE CHIEF JUSTICE OF CANADA, THE SPEAKER OF THE SENATE, THE SPEAKER OF THE HOUSE OF COMMONS AND THE LEADER OF THE OPPOSITION
speechtext:
This item seems to be a new departure in that it is a subvention for an air service. I am not quarrelling with the vote.
I think it was needed for that particular service. But is it to be the policy in future that subventions will be paid for air services?

speechtext: I do not think I could answer that question in the affirmative. All I can say is that this policy is authorized under the Aeronautics Act. speechtext:
Mr. Chairman, I said earlier today that my constituency was one of the orphan children of the Department of Transport. The minister might have thought I was exaggerating our unfortunate position, but 1 think after he has heard the brief statement I am about to make he will realize I was not overcritical.
My county of Gloucester is the most populous rural constituency in New Brunswick, with a population of 57,489. We have about 150 miles of line of the Canadian National Railways throughout the county, and I think we hold a record in not having one safety signal at any of our level railway crossings in the whole county. I do not know of any other constituency in New Brunswick without a safety device at any level crossing. I bring this matter to the attention of the minister so that he may make a note of it and remedy what I consider to be a dangerous and most unique situation in that province.

maintopic: ANNOUNCEMENT OF APPOINTMENT OF THE CHIEF JUSTICE OF CANADA, THE SPEAKER OF THE SENATE, THE SPEAKER OF THE HOUSE OF COMMONS AND THE LEADER OF THE OPPOSITION
speechtext: Do I understand the minister to say that in order to get a level crossing signal, or an underpass, the municipality must make application?

maintopic: ANNOUNCEMENT OF APPOINTMENT OF THE CHIEF JUSTICE OF CANADA, THE SPEAKER OF THE SENATE, THE SPEAKER OF THE HOUSE OF COMMONS AND THE LEADER OF THE OPPOSITION
speechtext: That is right.

maintopic: ANNOUNCEMENT OF APPOINTMENT OF THE CHIEF JUSTICE OF CANADA, THE SPEAKER OF THE SENATE, THE SPEAKER OF THE HOUSE OF COMMONS AND THE LEADER OF THE OPPOSITION
speechtext: Mr. Chairman, I believe greater consideration should be given to the matter of the elimination of level crossings. Our daily newspapers record accidents happening all across the country, and this condition is one that should be considered very seriously and carefully. I do not think any hon. member in the house would object to an expenditure much greater than the one indicated here. The increasing number of motor cars in our country is causing a more serious situation, and I suggest the government should give every consideration to increasing this vote, doubling or trebling it if necessary.

speechtext: This afternoon I referred to the situation in connection with the chairman of the Canadian maritime commission and suggested that someone should be appointed to this as a full-time post, rather than have the deputy minister act. The minister did not deal with that suggestion in his reply. Would he do so now?

maintopic: ANNOUNCEMENT OF APPOINTMENT OF THE CHIEF JUSTICE OF CANADA, THE SPEAKER OF THE SENATE, THE SPEAKER OF THE HOUSE OF COMMONS AND THE LEADER OF THE OPPOSITION
speechtext:
The hon. member made the same suggestion last year, and I am afraid I would have to make the same reply to him now that I did then, namely that I as minister, and I think I speak for the government,

Supply-Transport
feel that, with the deputy minister of transport as chairman of the maritime commission, I can at the moment receive better advice- and it will be noted that I say "at the moment"-than if an outside appointment were made.
I think at the time the former chairman was appointed there was a purpose behind it. namely that there was a great deal to do with reference to policy.
Until such time as it is possible to devise a policy in connection with the matter raised this afternoon by the hon. member, namely the position the government will take in so far as fast cargo vessels are concerned, their number and what assistance if any we should render to them, I think the interests of the maritime commission can best be served by the present incumbent. I certainly would not be disposed to recommend any change to the government at this time.

speechtext:
